issues.body: The malformed-object table includes a non-string body, but it still has no row with a valid positive issue number, an invalid title, and a null or absent body. Therefore changing the checked key tuple from `("title", "body")` to `("body",)` would leave the added suite green. That survivor matters because an accepted malformed title can conceal a legacy title-only alert and permit a duplicate to be created instead of refusing an incomplete dedupe view. The implementation itself correctly validates title; this is the same focused regression-coverage gap recorded in round 2.
issues.fix_hint: Add a wrapped full-`main()` failing-tick case such as `[{"number": 7, "title": 42, "body": null}]`, asserting rc 0, a sanitized warning, no payload echo, and no commands after `issue list`. Confirm that removing only `title` from `_usable_row`'s checked keys makes this case fail.
issues.title: The title-type half of the row guard still lacks an independent red test

verdict.summary: The production change remains sound and fail-closed: it validates the full row shape consumed by matching, rejects malformed listings wholesale before dedupe or recovery decisions, sanitizes the warning, and performs no mutation on a soft skip. The added full-main tests cover scalar and mixed rows, invalid bodies and issue numbers, both watchdog modes, and the valid null-body case. The prior round's sole minor coverage gap remains materially unchanged: no test independently makes the title-type check necessary. This does not establish a current production defect, so approval remains appropriate, but progress is stagnant relative to round 2.
